name: Creative Realities, Inc.

profile.description: Creative Realities is a digital signage and retail media technology company that designs, deploys, and manages digital display networks and owns its software stack (ReflectView CMS and AdLogic ad-serving, from the 2022 Reflect Systems merger) [3][4]. The acquisition of Cineplex Digital Media (CDM) drove Q2 2026 revenue to $21.5M from $13.0M, with CDM contributing $7.4M; annualized recurring revenue was ~$20.5M [1]. The company is small (~$29M market cap), carries $46.6M of debt, and has flagged risk around meeting upcoming debt obligations [1][5]. CEO Rick Mills has led the company through its pivot toward SaaS recurring revenue [3].

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Two acquisitions reshaped the company — the 2022 Reflect Systems merger added the AdLogic platform (nearly 50 million ads served daily) and the Cineplex Digital Media deal lifted Q2 2026 revenue 65% to $21.5M [1][3]. Revenue compounded at 26.8% annually from $17.5M (2020) to $57.2M (2025), mostly through M&A [6]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI savings were found; AI appears only in new executives' backgrounds [3]. Market Share (1/2): Post-CDM the company is a meaningful North American digital signage and retail media network operator, but no share data shows leadership [3]. Product Pipeline (0/2): Management promises a 'next generation SaaS platform' and record revenue (previously >$100M), but names no product with a launch date [1][3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP data shows no R&D expense in 2024–2025 [6].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Creative Realities describes itself as a software-first provider of digital signage and retail media technology — a description of the product, interchangeable with peers [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found, and filings show a new CFO and new insiders filing Form 3s, suggesting management turnover [5]. Insider Buying (2/2): CEO Richard C. Mills and CFO Tamra L. Koshewa bought shares on June 30, 2026 after a 12.1% quarterly price decline; aggregators put the CEO purchase at ~$700K (Form 4 verification recommended) — meaningful against a ~$29M market cap [5][7].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: HARD RULE — LIQUIDITY FLOOR APPLIED: average daily volume of 30,692 shares x $2.13 = ~$65,000 of daily dollar volume, far below the $1,000,000 floor, so Infrastructure = 0 regardless of other metrics [7]. For reference, the unadjusted weighted sum was 6.687 of 10: revenue growth of 65% YoY, a 5-year revenue CAGR of 26.8%, a forward P/E of 10.1, and PEG of 0.48 all score well, but ROE of -55%, profit margin of -29%, and D/E of 142% score poorly [6][7]. Debt stood at $46.6M at June 30, 2026, against ~$12.8M of revolver availability, and the company has flagged risk around meeting upcoming debt obligations [1][5].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Part of the business is physical — installing and servicing screens in retail, QSR, and theater venues — which AI cannot replace. But the software and content layer (CMS, ad-serving, content creation) is exposed: AI tools can automate creative production and commoditize signage CMS, and larger platforms can bundle AI-driven retail media capabilities [3][4]. No analyst coverage of CREX's AI risk was found, and the company has disclosed no AI product response, so the outcome is uncertain. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue is disclosed [1].

infinite_game.summary: Creative Realities is a micro-cap fighting for scale. Its strategy is acquisitions (Reflect, Cineplex Digital Media) financed with leverage, and its recent wins are revenue jumps from those deals, while the company posts net losses and flags debt-repayment risk [1][5]. CEO Mills says the CDM deal was 'about five years in the making,' and he and the CFO bought stock in June 2026 — signs of conviction [3][7]. But Sinek's infinite game requires a cause beyond survival, and there is little evidence of one yet.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The company's 'go big or go home' framing and positioning as a software-first retail media provider describe a business strategy, not a cause that serves people beyond customers [3]. No articulated vision of a better future state was found.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Filings show a new CFO and new insiders, and the C-suite was reshaped with a new CRO (late 2025) and CXO (March 2026) [3][5]. With repeated integrations and debt pressure, there is no evidence of a stable, high-trust culture.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Management's language — 'go big or go home', positioning as the digital signage leader after consolidation — frames competition as a scale contest, with no evidence of learning from rivals [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has shifted from a project-based signage installer to a SaaS and retail-media model with recurring revenue (~$20.5M ARR) [1][3]. The pivot is incremental and still in progress.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management pursued the multi-year CDM acquisition ('about five years in the making') and in February 2026 spent $200,000 to repurchase a warrant for 1,731,499 shares to reduce future dilution, putting long-term shareholder value ahead of near-term cash [3][5]. Insider purchases by the CEO and CFO after a price decline also show leaders backing the strategy with their own money [7].

investment_thesis: The bull case for Creative Realities is a transformed, larger company. The Cineplex Digital Media acquisition lifted Q2 2026 revenue to $21.5M (+65%) and adjusted EBITDA to $2.0M from $1.1M, and management expects Q3 to be the largest revenue quarter in company history, with Q4 higher still [1]. Gross margin should improve in the second half as SaaS and service revenue grows. The AdLogic and ReflectView stack gives CREX ownership of its retail-media technology [3][4]. At a ~$29M market cap with a forward P/E of 10.1 and PEG of 0.48, any execution success could re-rate the stock, and CEO and CFO insider buying in June 2026 signals management conviction [7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is balance-sheet stress and illiquidity. The company reported a $4.2M net loss in Q2 2026 and an $11.4M net loss for the first half; operating loss widened to $2.7M [1][5]. Debt is $46.6M against ~$12.8M of revolver availability, and an 8-K flagged risk to 'our ability to satisfy our upcoming debt obligations' [1][5]. ROE is -55% and profit margin -29% [7]. Average daily dollar volume of ~$65K is far below IOWN's $1M liquidity floor, making the stock untradeable at portfolio scale [7].
key_catalysts: Record H2 2026 revenue: management guides Q3 to be the largest revenue quarter in company history and Q4 to exceed Q3, as CDM contributes a full run-rate [1]
Margin mix shift: rising SaaS and service revenue (ARR ~$20.5M) should lift gross margin in H2 2026 and move adjusted EBITDA (Q2: $2.0M) toward positive net income [1]
Debt refinancing: refinancing the $46.6M debt load would remove the going-concern-style overhang flagged in company filings [1][5]
key_risks: Debt obligations: $46.6M of debt with only ~$12.8M of revolver capacity and an explicit filing warning about meeting upcoming obligations could force dilutive equity raises [1][5]
Persistent losses: H1 2026 net loss of $11.4M and Q2 operating loss of $2.7M show integration costs outpacing revenue gains [1][5]
Illiquidity and micro-cap volatility: ~30,700 shares (~$65K) trade daily, far below IOWN's $1M floor, and the stock fell 12.1% in the quarter before insider purchases [7]
